title: QBR Narrative — LumenEdge Health (Q1 2026)
body:
Purpose: a tight, account-specific narrative for the upcoming Q1 2026 QBR with LumenEdge Health. Use this as the facilitator script + speaker notes mapped to the slide outline. This draft is intentionally conversational — will be converted into a slide deck and a one-page exec summary.

Context and objectives:
- Customer: LumenEdge Health (regional provider network focusing on outpatient clinics and chronic care programs).
- Redwood relationship: On hosted API plan, started pilot (Feb 2025) -> production (Aug 2025) for triage-assist and patient summary generation.
- Current ARR influence: mid-market seat, upsell opportunity tied to Dedicated reserved capacity and longer-term Private deployment for PHI workloads.
- QBR goals: 1) demonstrate clear business impact (ops time saved, throughput improvements), 2) surface risks and mitigation, 3) align on renewal and roadmap asks, 4) agree next steps for Dedicated evaluation and SOC 2/KMS timeline.

High-level narrative arc (what we want them to feel):
- Gratitude: recognize quick adoption by clinical ops and the fast cycle from pilot -> production.
- Value: show concrete KPIs (time saved per case, latency improvements) and link to clinician satisfaction.
- Confidence: highlight reliability metrics and recent runbooks that reduced incidents.
- Partnership: propose concrete next steps (Dedicated POC, evaluation window, security sign-offs) and co-owned success metrics for renewal.

Key metrics to show (data pulls to validate before final deck):
- Average tokens per request: 1,450 (monthly avg) — verify Feb 2026 sample.
- Median latency (p95): 420ms on hosted API for triage-assist flows.
- Throughput: 1,200 requests/day peak, 450/day baseline.
- Clinician time saved: pilot surveys report ~12 min saved per patient summary (n=120).
- Error rate: user-visible hallucination incidents flagged: 0.8% (down from 1.7% in Q4 2025).
- Cost trend: cost-per-summary reduced 18% after batching and KV-caching recommendations.

Renewal posture and target:
- Current contract: Hosted API, month-to-month with committed credits through May 2026.
- Renewal target: convert to 12-month Dedicated reserved capacity SKU by June 2026 with 20% uplift in committed spend.
- Success criteria for switch: sustained p95 latency <= 500ms under peak, SOC2 attestation window aligned, proof that Dedicated POC reduces unit cost by >=25% in a 30-day test.

Open questions to confirm before meeting:
- Legal: Is there a specific KMS/HSM vendor required by their security team? (Rina to confirm).
- Product: Which additional endpoints (embeddings for document search) do they plan to roll out in next 90 days?
- Ops: Are there internal SLAs LumenEdge expects for on-call response if Dedicated is used?

Audience mapping and recommended attendees from LumenEdge:
- Executive sponsor: VP of Digital Transformation (primary decision maker).
- Technical champion: Lead ML Engineer (day-to-day integrator).
- Compliance: InfoSec manager (contract/controls).
- Clinical ops rep: Senior RN who led pilot adoption (user story).

Tone and pitfalls to avoid:
- Avoid deep infra jargon in exec slides — emphasize business outcomes and predictable economics.
- Don’t overpromise on timelines for Private deployment until KMS/legal gating items are validated.
- Be transparent about the handful of hallucination incidents and show remediation steps we took.

Appendix material to attach: recent incident timeline (Jan–Feb 2026), sample clinician survey results, cost model spreadsheet (before/after batching), technical brief for Dedicated POC (3-week test plan).
slides_outline: Slide 2: Where we started — Pilot summary & timeline (Feb–Aug 2025)
Slide 3: Business impact — Time saved, throughput, clinician feedback (KPIs)
Slide 4: Reliability and performance — p95 latency, error reduction, uptime
Slide 5: Recent improvements — KV caching, batching, reranking thresholds
Slide 6: Risk & mitigation — hallucination incidents, mitigation runbook
Slide 7: Cost story — hosted cost trends and Dedicated POC hypothesis
Slide 8: Proposed trajectory — Dedicated POC plan, success metrics, timeline
Slide 9: Ask & decision points — renewal cadence, security checklist, POC sign-off
Slide 10: Next steps & owners — clear action items, dates, contacts
talking_points: Opening: Thank you — note rapid adoption and the RN-led champion who pushed integration live.
Business impact: Clinicians report ~12 min saved per patient summary. Translate to FTE equivalent for the network.
Performance: p95 under 500ms; explain what that means for triage flow and clinician context switches.
Reliability: Describe the incident in Jan and the corrective steps — automated retries and prompt evaluations.
Cost: Show the before/after with batching and why Dedicated is likely to reduce per-unit cost further.
Security ask: Outline SOC2 / KMS milestones and ask them for timeline input from their InfoSec team.
Decision: Propose a 30-day Dedicated POC with a clear roll-in milestone that leads to a June renewal decision.
action_items: Ethan: Pull Feb 2026 token and latency distribution by endpoint (due 2026-02-22)
Rina: Confirm KMS vendor constraints with Legal and populate security checklist (due 2026-02-25)
Noah: Draft Dedicated POC runbook (3-week plan + success metrics) and cost model (due 2026-02-28)
Maya: Prepare one-page exec summary and send meeting invite to LumenEdge VP (due 2026-03-03)
risks: Security gating: If KMS/HSM is incompatible, Private/Dedicated timeline shifts >60 days.
Adoption risk: Clinical ops may deprioritize expansion if short-term SLA breaches reoccur.
Budget risk: Finance at LumenEdge could push back on uplift without clearer unit cost proof.
Competitive risk: Another provider could pitch a faster time-to-compliance for PHI workloads.
exec_summary_one_liner: LumenEdge is seeing measurable clinician time savings and reliability gains; conversion to Dedicated with a 30-day POC is the clearest path to securing a 12-month committed renewal by June 2026.
notes_to_self: Keep slide deck to 10 slides, rehearse p95 latency explanation with graphs, bring 1–2 customer quotes from RN champion. Leave 10 minutes for security Q&A.
